# Tegla Loroupe
## Full Biography
Tegla Loroupe, born 9 May 1973 in Kapsait, Kenya, established herself as a pioneer in distance running by becoming the first African woman to hold the marathon world record. Holding that title from 19 April 1998 until 30 September 2001, she redefined international standards while navigating a challenging path from a childhood of rural labor to global prominence.

# Tegla Loroupe
## Early Development and Athletic Emergence
Raised in a polygamous household within the West Pokot District, Loroupe began her education at six years old, running ten kilometers to school daily. Despite initial resistance from Athletics Kenya, which dismissed her due to her slight build, she proved her capability by winning a cross-country barefoot race in 1988. By 1989, she secured her first pair of professional running shoes, subsequently placing 28th at the IAAF World Cross Country Championships.
![Image 10: 25th Laureus World Sports Awards - Red Carpet - Tegla Loroupe - 240422 183851](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:FilePath/25th_Laureus_World_Sports_Awards_-_Red_Carpet_-_Tegla_Loroupe_-_240422_183851_%28cropped%29.jpg?width=800)
25th Laureus World Sports Awards - Red Carpet - Tegla Loroupe - 240422 183851

# Tegla Loroupe
## Professional Marathon and Track Success
Loroupe achieved significant victories at the New York City Marathon, winning the event twice. Her career included world records for the 25 and 30 kilometer distances, as well as the One Hour running record of 18,340 meters. She secured multiple wins at the Rotterdam, Berlin, London, and Rome marathons. At the 2000 Sydney Olympics, despite suffering from food poisoning, she completed both the marathon and 10,000-meter races, placing 13th and 5th respectively.

# Tegla Loroupe
## Peace Initiatives and Humanitarian Work
Using sports as a vehicle for conflict resolution, Loroupe established the Tegla Loroupe Peace Foundation and the Peace Through Sports initiative. She launched the Tegla Loroupe Peace Academy and an orphanage in Kapenguria to support local children. Her efforts include organizing annual Peace Marathons in Kenya, Uganda, and Sudan, which have encouraged nomadic tribes and warriors to cease fighting. In 2016, she organized the Refugee Team for the Summer Olympics in Rio.

Title: Olympian Loroupe Sets Example with UN Honour
Chunks: 0,1
2 | 11 | 2016
Tegla Loroupe exemplified all that it means to be an Olympian as she accepted the prestigious honour of being named United Nations Person of the Year in Kenya.
At a ceremony at the UN office in Nairobi, Loroupe was honoured for her work championing the ability of refugees to participate at the Rio 2016 Olympic Games as well as her leadership in taking peace to conflict zones in Africa.
As Chef de Mission of the first ever Refugee Olympic Team, Loroupe was instrumental in petitioning the International Olympic Committee (IOC) to allow refugees the opportunity to compete in Rio. As a result of her efforts, ten refugees from Syria, Congo, Ethiopia and South Sudan, including five who were residing at the Kakuma refugee camp in her native Kenya, were selected for the Games, competing under the IOC banner for the first time.
Loroupe, a former marathon world record holder, has long been a powerful advocate for peace. In 2006 she was named a UN Ambassador for Sport and is currently a member of Peace and Sport’s Champions for Peace, a group of athletes who seek to use the power of sport to bring about unity.
Through the Tegla Loroupe Peace Foundation, which was established in 2003 to support peace building efforts in Kenya and the greater Horn of Africa, Loroupe uses sport and education programmes to help those in need. In 2014 she organised the first peace run in Kakuma Refugee Camp to commemorate World Refugee Day and her athletic training facility for refugees in Ngong Nairobi continues to train talented refugees in athletics and many other sports with the aim of enabling them to compete internationally.
Loroupe was also one of five Olympians honoured in World Olympians Association’s Olympians for Life project which was launched at the Olympians Reunion Centre by EY during the Rio 2016 Olympic Games.
**WOA President **Joël**Bouzou** said:
“Tegla Loroupe is an inspiration to us all and a worthy recipient of this important honour from the UN in Kenya. As an Olympian she embodies the Olympic spirit, setting an example as an ambassador for peace and a powerful advocate for the rights of both refugees and women.

“WOA extends its warmest congratulations to Tegla for this richly deserved award. We look forward to following her work as she continues to serve society, acting as a role model to other Olympians by demonstrating the power of sport to change lives, bring together divided communities and build peace.”

2 | 11 | 2016
Tegla Loroupe exemplified all that it means to be an Olympian as she accepted the prestigious honour of being named United Nations Person of the Year in Kenya.
At a ceremony at the UN office in Nairobi, Loroupe was honoured for her work championing the ability of refugees to participate at the Rio 2016 Olympic Games as well as her leadership in taking peace to conflict zones in Africa.
As Chef de Mission of the first ever Refugee Olympic Team, Loroupe was instrumental in petitioning the International Olympic Committee (IOC) to allow refugees the opportunity to compete in Rio. As a result of her efforts, ten refugees from Syria, Congo, Ethiopia and South Sudan, including five who were residing at the Kakuma refugee camp in her native Kenya, were selected for the Games, competing under the IOC banner for the first time.
Loroupe, a former marathon world record holder, has long been a powerful advocate for peace. In 2006 she was named a UN Ambassador for Sport and is currently a member of Peace and Sport’s Champions for Peace, a group of athletes who seek to use the power of sport to bring about unity.
Through the Tegla Loroupe Peace Foundation, which was established in 2003 to support peace building efforts in Kenya and the greater Horn of Africa, Loroupe uses sport and education programmes to help those in need. In 2014 she organised the first peace run in Kakuma Refugee Camp to commemorate World Refugee Day and her athletic training facility for refugees in Ngong Nairobi continues to train talented refugees in athletics and many other sports with the aim of enabling them to compete internationally.
Loroupe was also one of five Olympians honoured in World Olympians Association’s Olympians for Life project which was launched at the Olympians Reunion Centre by EY during the Rio 2016 Olympic Games.
**WOA President **Joël**Bouzou** said:
“Tegla Loroupe is an inspiration to us all and a worthy recipient of this important honour from the UN in Kenya. As an Olympian she embodies the Olympic spirit, setting an example as an ambassador for peace and a powerful advocate for the rights of both refugees and women.
texts.1: “WOA extends its warmest congratulations to Tegla for this richly deserved award. We look forward to following her work as she continues to serve society, acting as a role model to other Olympians by demonstrating the power of sport to change lives, bring together divided communities and build peace.”

**2000 Olympic Games in Sydney. She finished 5th in the 10,000m**
**and 13th in the marathon. As a marathon runner she won the event**
**in London (2000), New York 1995 & 1994 and Rotterdam 1995 & 1997.**
